units.meaning: Provides the section title establishing that 8 FAM 403.1-4 addresses material discrepancies, also referred to as major name changes, containing no independent operative rule.

source_spans.quote: 8 FAM 403.1-4 Material Discrepancies (Major name changes)

units.meaning: Provides administrative version and date metadata for the document section, containing no operative legal or procedural requirement.
Defines a 'material discrepancy' as any name change that is not classified as immaterial pursuant to 8 FAM 403.1-5.

source_spans.quote: A material discrepancy is any name change that is not defined as immaterial in 8 FAM 403.1-5.

units.meaning: The applicant is required to provide an explanation for any material discrepancies between the name stated on the application and the name appearing in the evidence of citizenship/non-citizen nationality and the evidence of identity.

source_spans.quote: The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

units.meaning: Applicants must document any material discrepancies among the name recorded on the application, citizenship/non-citizen nationality evidence, or identity evidence by submitting at least one acceptable document listed in this section, subject to an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).

source_spans.quote: Material discrepancies between the name recorded on the application, the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality, or the evidence of identity must be documented by submission of one or more of the documents listed in this section (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C)).

units.meaning: Exceptions to the mandatory submission of the documents listed in this section apply for married names under 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).

source_spans.quote: (see an exception for married names in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C))

units.meaning: Adjudicators must review all submitted evidence of material name changes for signs of counterfeiting or alteration pursuant to 8 FAM 201.1.

source_spans.quote: Evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration (see 8 FAM 201.1)

units.meaning: An applicant is prohibited from continuing to use a previous name after undergoing a material name change, unless the name change documentation explicitly authorizes the continued use of that previous name.

source_spans.quote: The applicant may not continue to use a previous name after a material name change unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name (see 8 FAM 403.1-6 regarding “known as” names).

units.meaning: Expresses the foundational principle that an applicant's name is an integral component of identity, providing context for identity evidence rules without setting an explicit directive.

source_spans.quote: The applicant's name is an integral part of her/his identity.

units.meaning: Under 22 CFR 51.23(c) and Department guidance, passport personnel are authorized to require evidence of identity to establish the name that best identifies the applicant.

source_spans.quote: Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:

units.meaning: When an applicant applies on Form DS-11 more than one year after a material name change without updating their ID, passport staff must suspend the application and request acceptable ID issued in the new name.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.
Consequently, under 22 CFR 51.23(c), evidence of identity might be required in accordance with Department guidance to establish the name that best identifies the applicant:

units.meaning: Passport personnel may issue a limited-validity passport in the requested name when an applicant who had a material name change over a year prior lacks updated ID, if urgent or emergency travel does not allow enough time to request and receive updated ID.

source_spans.quote: If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name;

If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.

units.meaning: States the general expectation that an applicant will require their name change documentation in order to update the name on their identification.

source_spans.quote: The applicant generally will need the name change documentation to change the name on her/his ID.

units.meaning: Staff are required to fully notate name change documentation, explicitly recording that it was 'seen and returned,' before returning it to the applicant along with an information request letter (IRL).

source_spans.quote: You must fully notate the name change documentation prior to returning the documentation, including that the documentation was "seen and returned," to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL);

units.meaning: Applicants who apply on Form DS-11 within one year of a material name change are exempt from the requirement to submit an ID reflecting the new name.

source_spans.quote: Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name.

units.meaning: If an applicant who changed their name within one year of applying on Form DS-11 has not yet updated their ID, they are required to submit their name change documentation.

source_spans.quote: However, if the ID has not yet been changed, they must submit their name change documentation.
Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name.
